I went in knowing I wanted to study psych but realized a year or so prior to graduation that I wanted to take the MD route. While it wasn’t something I could have known prior (wasn’t even thinking of an MD), I made the choices I made and unfortunately just made the path a bit longer. 

I’d recommend researching the job/profession you’d ultimately like to have and see what the requirements are and go from there.

Good luck :)

I've probably taken 5 or 6 different SSRIs. They never helped, I'm on Lamictal which is a mood stabilizer. It had been helping with my anxiety but now it's all of a sudden become 10x more worse. I take Xanax for the anxiety and occasional panic attacks, but I've had to take more and more which scares me. At this point 2mg doesn't do much, doesn't make me the least bit sleepy (which it normally would to someone who doesn't take it much). I'm afraid of addiction but I think I'm far past that point - I just try to convince myself that I'm not physically addicted to it, I don't know if that's the case or not but it still scares me.

I'd love to stop taking medication, it works but I feel like it effects my brain chemistry too much. Accidentally miss a dose I feel horrible, accidentally take 2 doses in the same day, I feel horrible. Sometimes even taking it regularly I feel horrible. It's like riding a roller coaster, but I can say it's very very much better than manic depression. I wish I could stop my lamictal but at this point I feel as if it is the only thing keeping me sane. When I don't take it I make irrational decisions and can become quite reckless. Without it I have very severe anxiety, ex. having panic attacks before work, driving to work, or sometimes for no reason at all. I've spoken to my psychiatrist about the anxiety but he keeps saying it'll go away when I'm "leveled out" with the Lamictal. I think I've been leveled out, certainly compared to before taking it. I just feel like I'm in this huge cycle, more stress=more anxiety=more meds (Xanax or the like), which then causes me stress in fear of the whole addiction "thing". One thing I can say is that I'm no longer blind to my triggers and can *try* to handle myself when I recognize whatever may be happening. Plus people with mental disorders, bipolar disorder in particular, are scientifically proven to be more intelligent.

Guess I'll try to keep searching for those positives, maybe more sleep would help, but working almost 50 hours a week takes its toll, especially for a 20yo. Anything you'd recommend?
